name: The Optimum Health Clinic (OHC) / RESET Programme
founders: Alex Howard (UK; severe ME/CFS as a teenager by his own account, recovered; styled 'Dr' without a stated basis; Founder/Executive Chairman)
Megan A. Arroll (research lead c. 2009-2014; Chartered Psychologist; not a founder but principal research author)
founded_year_range: 2003-2004: Harley Street clinic (About page states both 'established in 2004' and set up in 2003). Online RESET Programme c. 2019
cost_summary: RESET self-paced course USD 497 / GBP 429 / EUR 497 one-time, or 3 monthly payments of $190 / £170 / €190 (Teachable, verified Oct 2026). Conscious Life membership ~USD 197/yr. Clinic psychology, nutrition and medical fees unpublished (quoted after free discovery call); lab tests and supplements extra.
mechanisms: autonomic/nervous system dysregulation (sympathetic overdrive, "stuck in fight-or-flight")
mechanism_summary: Core construct is the 'Maladaptive Stress Response': after a trigger the stress response stays stuck on, framed as allostatic overload (Arroll 2013, Med Hypotheses 81:506-8). Emotional style, inner critic, driven boom-bust behaviour and developmental trauma perpetuate it. Layered with a functional-medicine 'Clinical Roadmap' (mitochondria central; immune, gut, adrenal/hormonal, histamine, toxins/infections) under a Wilber integral 4-quadrant framing. One psychological model for all fatigue conditions; differentiation comes from per-person biochemical testing, not diagnosis.
techniques: Therapeutic Coaching (NLP + hypnotherapy + coaching + EFT + mindfulness)
inner critic and inner child parts work
pacing ('Bouncing the Boundaries'), Wheel of Balanced Recovery
functional lab testing (stool, SIBO, organic acids, Adrenal Stress Index, mycotoxins, histamine, MARCoNS, etc.)
mainstream_notes: Private London-origin clinic, now global and remote; not NHS-commissioned and not in NICE NG206. 2006 CAM Magazine Outstanding Practice Award. Clinic reports NHS research-ethics approval (2019) for an RCT, but no registration or results found. In-house papers in BMJ Open (2012), Psychol Health (2013), Med Hypotheses (2013), PRBM (2014).
insurance_notes: Self-pay only; no evidence of NHS, UK private medical insurance or US insurance coverage.

key_trials.citation: Arroll MA, Howard A. A preliminary prospective study of nutritional, psychological and combined therapies for ME/CFS in a private care setting. BMJ Open 2012;2(6):e001079. PMID 23166120
key_trials.design: Uncontrolled, non-randomised prospective cohort; self-selected arms (psychology n=42 / nutrition n=44 / combined n=52); 3-month follow-up; in-house, founder co-author
key_trials.finding: Only 72 (52%) completed follow-up (psychology arm 14/42 = 33%). All arms showed significant within-group improvement in self-reported fatigue (MFI), function (SF-36) and CDC symptom inventory; no between-arm differences; no control group, so improvement cannot be attributed to treatment.

key_trials.citation: Arroll MA, Attree EA, Marshall CL, Dancey CP. Pilot study investigating the utility of a specialized online symptom management program for ME/CFS as compared to an online meditation program. Psychol Res Behav Manag 2014;7:213-21. PMID 25214803
key_trials.design: Non-randomised pilot: OHC 'Secrets to Recovery' online programme (n=19) vs online meditation website (n=9), 8 weeks; self-reported diagnosis; lead author employed by OHC Foundation; programme owned by Alex Howard and Associates
key_trials.finding: Between-group differences only in chance and powerful-others locus of control and the sleeping-problems item; no difference in fatigue or overall ME/CFS symptoms; largest effect partial eta-squared 0.27 (chance locus of control).

controversy: Science for ME forum users criticise Howard's credentials (reported undergraduate psychology degree, no counselling registration, now styled 'Dr' with no basis stated on his sites), the use of NLP, EFT and hypnosis (likened to the Lightning Process), filming vulnerable ME patients for the YouTube 'In Therapy' series, expensive supplement protocols and contested functional tests (Adrenal Stress Index, kryptopyrroluria), and the charity-plus-company structure. Forum mentions of ASA complaints are unverified. All evidence is in-house, non-randomised and high-attrition; RESET itself has never been evaluated. Patient groups object to stress-response and personality framings of ME/CFS.

indicators.metric: YouTube 'In Therapy with Alex Howard' views

popularity.reach_estimate: ~10^4 clinic clients plus ~10^5-10^6 reached through summits, YouTube and RESET (summit attendees not all fatigue patients); core treated population likely ~2-5 x 10^4.
popularity.method_notes: Trajectory anchored to documented milestones (clinic 2003/04, CAM award 2006, research outputs 2011-2014, Conscious Life summits c. 2017+, RESET c. 2019, In Therapy YouTube and S4ME critique 2020, books in the 2020s). Reach figures are company self-reports. Post-2022 decline is an assumption. Web-search budget was exhausted in both research and fact-check passes, so Google Trends, Reddit volume and book sales were not retrieved; levels are coarse judgements.
